topic.name: The Area of a General Triangle

question.text: The area of ​​the triangle $\triangle ABC$ is $\dfrac{21}{4} \text{ cm}^2.$ Find $AC.$
question.explanation:
The formula for the area of the triangle is \[ \mathcal{A}=\dfrac{1}{2}bc\sin{A}, \] where $\angle{A}$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$

Here \begin{align} c & = AB = 3 \text{ cm},\\ b & = AC,\\ m \angle A & = 30^\circ. \end{align}

Since \[ \sin{30^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1}{2}, \] we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows: \begin{align} \mathcal{A} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot c \cdot \sin A \\[5pt] \dfrac{21}{4} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot 3 \cdot \sin{30^\circ} \\[5pt] \dfrac{21}{4} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot b \cdot 3 \cdot \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \right) \\[5pt] \dfrac{21}{4} & = \dfrac{3 b}{4} \\[5pt] 3 b & = 21 \\[5pt] b & = 7 \text{ cm}. \end{align}

We conclude that $AC = 7\textrm{cm}.$

example.title: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle

question.text: Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
question.explanation:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $\triangle ABD$ and $\triangle BDC$ (see the illustration below).

First we find the area for $\triangle ABD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABD} &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 10 \cdot 8 \cdot \sin 75^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 40 \cdot \sin 75^\circ\\[5pt] &\approx 38.637, \end{align*} rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Now we find the area for $\triangle BCD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{BDC} &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 5 \cdot 12 \cdot \sin 67.2^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 30 \cdot \sin 67.2^\circ \\[5pt] &\approx 27.656, \end{align*} rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD\mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} &= \mathcal{A}_{ABD}+\mathcal{A}_{BDC} \\ &= 38.637 + 27.656 \\ &= 66.293 \end{align*}

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $66.$

example.title: Calculating the Area of a Quadrilateral

question.text: The area of $ABCD$ is $52 \text{ in}^2.$ What is the area of $\triangle BCD$ rounded to the nearest integer?
question.explanation:
Let's start by finding the area of $\triangle ABD.$ We get

\begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} & = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot AB \cdot AD \cdot \sin{A}\\[5pt] &= {\dfrac 1 2} \cdot 9 \cdot 16 \cdot \sin 66^ \circ \\[5pt] &= 72 \cdot \sin 66^\circ \\[5pt] & = 65.775 \ldots\\[5pt] & \approx 66 \textrm{ in}^2, \end{align*} rounded to the nearest integer.

The difference of the areas of $\triangle ABD$ and the quadrilateral $ABCD$ gives the area of $\triangle BCD.$ Therefore, \begin{align*} \mathcal{A}_{\triangle BCD} & = \mathcal{A}_{\triangle ABD} - \mathcal{A}_{ABCD} \\[3pt] & = 66 - 52 \\[3pt] & = 14\, \textrm{ in}^2. \end{align*}
